_comment:
"If you've dealt arcane damage this turn, this gets +2{p}."

The release notes govern the ability type: 'Whether you've dealt arcane damage this turn is checked while this is attacking on the combat chain' is an always-checking condition, so this is a WHILE_STATIC re-evaluated on RECALC_ATTACK_POWER - NOT a TRIGGERED ON_ATTACK pump (same lesson as Aggressive Pounce; the red sibling's triage reached the same conclusion). A TRIGGERED ON_ATTACK pump would freeze the answer at attack declaration and miss arcane damage dealt between declaration and damage calculation, which the second release note explicitly says must count.

EVENT_THIS_TURN event=damage qualifier=arcane reads the markers deal_damage records against the DEALING player once damage is final - past replacements and cancellation, amount > 0 (effect_keywords.py ~503-509) - so fully-prevented arcane damage does not count. player defaults to SELF = this card's controller: 'YOU'VE dealt arcane damage'. This exact condition shape is documented for this wording at condition_types.py ~1047.

WHILE_STATIC re-fires on every recalculation (declaration, after reactions, at damage calculation), so arcane damage dealt earlier in the turn or before the damage step yields +2{p} during damage calculation - matching release notes two and three. MODIFY_ATTACK under a recalc-type event applies transiently in the stage-8 window and does not accumulate across recalcs (effect_types.py ~4070-4080).

SOURCE_IS_ATTACK scopes the buff to this card's own attack (Savage Claw pattern). Strictly belt-and-braces here - an Action - Attack is only walked by the recalc listener as combat.attack_card - but it guards against future dispatch broadening and costs nothing.

+2{p} is the blue printing; red/yellow siblings differ only in the amount per family convention and are not in this batch.
